title: Why You Can't Remember Being a Baby
description: You were there for your first steps... so why can't you remember them? The science of infantile amnesia in under a minute. #facts #brain #psychology #science

scenes.headline: 0 MEMORIES
scenes.text: You were there for your first steps, your first word, your first birthday. And you remember none of it.

scenes.headline: AGE 3
scenes.text: Scientists call it infantile amnesia. For most adults, the earliest memory comes from around age three.

scenes.headline: BUT WAIT
scenes.text: But here's the strange part. Babies do remember. Three month olds can remember how to kick a toy mobile, days later.
In 2025, Yale scientists scanned babies' brains, and saw the memory center storing new memories from about one year old.

scenes.headline: REWIRED
scenes.sub: new neurons pave over old paths
scenes.text: So why do they vanish? One idea: a baby's brain grows so fast that new neurons rewire the old paths, like paving over a trail.

scenes.headline: NO WORDS
scenes.text: Another idea: you didn't have words yet, so your memories have no label to search for.

scenes.headline: LOCKED
scenes.text: And the twist? In mice, scientists have switched lost baby memories back on. Your first birthday might still be in there. You just lost the key.

scenes.headline: FOLLOW
scenes.text: Follow for more things your brain never told you.
